label: Q03
question: Can a full datetime_start_utc be derived for each tow? Source (Sheet1, 'Final Data') only has Month/Year/Time (HH.MM) -- no Day -- and Time's UTC-vs-local status is unconfirmed.
context: No Day column was found in Sheet1, so no full calendar date seemed derivable from the file at all. An interim approach (nearest-neighbor site_key match feeding match_by_site_datetime() with a placeholder mid-month date) was drafted and then explicitly reverted -- untested/too fragile, calcofi_bottle dropped from the dependency list entirely, reverted to source-only year/month/hour/minute fields with no datetime_start_utc.
answer: Resolved by finding a real per-tow date: the SAME workbook (bb9217084g_1_1.xlsx) has a hidden 'Original' sheet (raw field log, distinct from the curated Sheet1) with a genuine Date of Tow column, separate Start hour/Start Minute integer fields, and an explicit Time Zone column (PST/PDT, i.e. genuinely DST-aware, not assumed) -- joinable to Sheet1 by CruiseID+Tow, no placeholder dates or nearest-neighbor matching needed. Cross-validated against Sheet1's own Time field for all 102 tows: 80 match exactly; 21 more are explained as a Sheet1 decimal-entry typo (single-digit minutes lost their leading zero -- provably wrong, since 3 of the 21 decode to 60/80/90 minutes, impossible on a 24hr clock -- Original's minute used instead); the remaining 15 (all of cruise 1110, 2011-10) have a genuine unexplained +1hr conflict on hour only, not resolved -- see Q06 (NEW).

label: Q05
question: Can the packed Station value (e.g. '93.120') be reliably decomposed into CalCOFI line/station for site_key resolution?
context: CalCOFI standard lines are non-integer (93.3, 86.7, not 93/87), and 3-digit stations lose a trailing zero to Excel float storage ('93.120' vs float 93.11 -- ambiguous as station 120 vs 11); direct parsing is unreliable.
answer: Resolved without parsing Station at all. Every tow already has real lat/lon (LatFinal/LongFinal), so site_key is derived from a spatial match against the same grid reference add_spatial already uses for grid_key: once grid_key is assigned via assign_grid_key(), site_key is looked up as that cell's line/station labels (grid.line || ',' || grid.station). This is a different mechanism than the nearest-neighbor-against-calcofi_bottle-Cast attempt tried and reverted earlier (too fragile/untested) -- it reuses the grid polygon reference already loaded for grid_key, not a point-to-point nearest-neighbor match, and does not reintroduce calcofi_bottle as a runtime dependency. station_raw is kept verbatim alongside site_key for anyone auditing against the original file.

label: Q06
question: For cruise 1110 (2011-10) specifically, all 15 tows show the 'Original' sheet's Start hour = Sheet1's Time hour + 1 (mod 24), with minutes agreeing exactly every time. Which is correct?
context: Discovered while resolving Q03. Not a DST-transition artifact -- October 2011 is entirely PDT per Original's own Time Zone column, no PST rows in this cruise. Both hour values are independently valid (0-23), so nothing in the source disproves either one.
answer: Not resolved. Currently defaulted to Sheet1's hour (the curated 'Final Data' sheet the rest of this ingest is built from) for these 15 rows, flagged via a new hour_source_conflict column on mesopelagic_fish_tow -- a judgment call pending confirmation, not a resolved fact.
